humanities_role_explanation: Historical newspaper articles (BLN600) supply the items, but the competence tested is generic post-OCR text correction (OCR error repair via seq2seq/LLM), not disciplinary humanities competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only: noisy OCR text sequences as input, human re-keyed transcription as target. Images are not shown to the models.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Post-OCR correction framed as sequence-to-sequence NMT (BART) or prompt-based instruction following (Llama 2: 'Fix the OCR errors in the provided text'). Error types discussed: substitution, insertion, deletion, misnamed entities, hallucination.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Single task (post-OCR correction) on a single dataset (BLN600); no new benchmark is introduced.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Llama 2 7B and 13B (LoRA instruction-tuned) compared with BART base/large.

quantitative_metrics.note: Percentage reduction in character error rate (CER), averaged over five runs.

summary: The paper instruction-tunes Llama 2 (7B, 13B) with LoRA for post-OCR correction of BLN600, a corpus of 19th-century British newspaper articles, and compares it to fine-tuned BART. Llama 2 13B substantially outperforms BART and is more data-efficient with limited training data.
key_findings: Llama 2 13B achieves a 54.51% CER reduction vs 23.30% for BART large (14.60% for BART base, 43.26% for Llama 2 7B). Llama 2 performs strongly even with small training subsets, whereas BART improves substantially with more data.
gold_upstream: BLN600 (Booth et al., 2024): OCR excerpts from British Library Newspapers with manually re-keyed human transcriptions from the source images; further production details not described in this paper.
facets_explanation: Reference texts are the manually re-keyed human transcriptions from BLN600, an existing dataset by overlapping authors (Booth et al. 2024). The paper does not describe annotator expertise or agreement. Scoring compares model output to a single reference via CER.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports 'Llama 2 13B 54.51' as percentage CER reduction (mean over five training and evaluation iterations), versus BART 400M 23.30. The metric is CER reduction, not a standard listed metric, hence 'other'. Training-set size comparison (six subsets of 80 samples) is a training-data ablation, not a format gap. No human baseline is given.

humanities_role.quote: Poor OCR quality continues to be a major obstacle for humanities scholars seeking to make use of digitised primary sources such as historical newspapers.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: By instruction-tuning Llama 2 and comparing it to a fine-tuned BART on BLN600

gold_source.quote: The dataset contains OCR excerpts from British Library Newspapers Parts I-II (1800-1900) (Gale, 2024), along with high-quality manually re-keyed human transcriptions from the source images.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: For each ground truth segment, the corresponding OCR text is then gathered using a search algorithm

answer_multiplicity.quote: computing the Levenshtein distance between the recognised text and the reference text
